question.problem:
Let $X$ be the outcome of rolling an unfair  four-sided die that follows the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below. What is $\text{Var}[X]?$

| $x$ | $-4$ | $-3$ | $-2$ | $-1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{5}{16}$ |
question.worked_solution:
We can compute the variance of a discrete random variable $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =(-4)\cdot f(-4)+(-3)\cdot f(-3)+(-2)\cdot f(-2)+(-1)\cdot f(-1) \\  & =(-4)(\frac{1}{2})+(-3)(\frac{1}{16})+(-2)(\frac{1}{8})+(-1)(\frac{5}{16}) \\  & =-\frac{11}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & =(-4)^{2}\cdot f(-4)+(-3)^{2}\cdot f(-3)+(-2)^{2}\cdot f(-2)+(-1)^{2}\cdot f(-1) \\  & =16(\frac{1}{2})+9(\frac{1}{16})+4(\frac{1}{8})+1(\frac{5}{16}) \\  & =\frac{75}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{75}{8}-{(-\frac{11}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{75}{8}-\frac{121}{16} \\  & =\frac{150}{16}-\frac{121}{16} \\  & =\frac{29}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
